courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Success in LAS for International Students
courses.description: Prepares international students for their transition to campus by examining expectations and focusing on the purpose and value of the higher education experience from a US perspective. Introduces critical concepts to know about academic programs, and engages students in planning their program of study as well as their personal and professional development. Serves as a complement to LAS 101 / LAS 102 / LAS 122 for students new to the US education system.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Design Your First Year Experience
courses.description: Design Your First Year Experience orients students to the academic environment at Illinois and establishes a useful framework for engaging in learning both inside and outside the classroom and articulating a purpose for their education. Using design-thinking, students explore campus resources, set goals for their academic, personal and professional development during their first year and make multiple (engagement) maps for reaching those goals.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to first-year students in LAS.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Transfer Advantage
courses.description: Introduction for first-term transfer students to the college and campus. Familiarizes transfer student with the resources available to them and helps them connect with other students and form a bond with the college.
courses.prereqText: For first-term LAS transfer students only.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: BLS Online Student Success
courses.description: Empowers first-term students in the online Bachelor of Liberal Studies program to thrive at Illinois. Students will learn about support services, connect with peers in the program, plan their transfer journey, and develop strategies for balancing academics and life. Tools are provided that will align academic and career experiences with students' unique goals. Approved for S/U grading only.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: First Year College Success
courses.description: Builds on the skills and information obtained in LAS 101 to create the toolbox needed to effectively explore academic possibilities. Enables students to successfully declare a major, as well as achieve and maintain academic excellence at Illinois and beyond.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Leadership and Society
courses.description: Engages first-year LAS honors students in the realms of citizenship, stewardship and leadership for the 21st century. En route to becoming competent and agile learners, first-year honors students experience an orientation to Illinois that fosters greater awareness and knowledge of campus resources and an examination of scholarly and personal leadership, global issues, and civic engagement. The course serves as a means for students to enhance their independence, cultural awareness and connection to community. Students work with a small cohort of peer scholars in a one-hour weekly graded session led by an upper-level LAS James Scholar peer mentor. Students are expected to work together and individually on projects involving community partners and campus groups. Assignments will incorporate the concept of service in connection with civic engagement.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Social Innovations for Global Challenges
courses.description: Real-world practice in problem-solving, cross-cultural communication, and organizational support. Applying a human-centered design framework, students, guided by professional mentors, develop innovative solutions to social challenges posed by local and global organizations. Students provide research and professional support to organizations and, in turn, develop the critical skills necessary to be impactful leaders in the global society and workforce. May be repeated in separate semesters to a maximum of 6 hours.
courses.prereqText: LAS first-year students accepted into the Global Leaders Program.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Undergraduate Open Seminar
courses.description: Topics will vary. See class schedule. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: International Collaborations for Global impact
courses.description: An experiential course designed to provide domestic and international students with real-world practice in problem-solving, cross-cultural communication, and organizational support. Applying a Human-Centered Design framework, students are trained to develop innovative solutions to social challenges that impact our world by collaborating with international organizations and partners. May be repeated in separate semesters to a maximum of 6 hours. Enrollment in LAS 205 for both the Fall and consecutive Spring term is a requirement for active participation in the LAS Global Leaders Program.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to LAS second-year students who have completed LAS 195 and are accepted into the Global Leaders Program.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Leadership and Social Change
courses.description: An examination of leadership from historical, political, and sociological perspectives through a study of how a natural disaster impacted a community within the United States. Participation in a community service trip during spring break may be required. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours, if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to LAS James Scholars Honors program students.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Writing Job Applications
courses.description: Theories and practical techniques of writing successful cover letters and resumes. Emphasizes adaptable communication and research skills, including use of career resources, investigation of potential employers, selection of appropriate jobs that fit students’ skills and interests, and targeting of resumes and cover letters to particular job applications.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Internship Experience
courses.description: Students follow a program of study and research through an approved internship. Written work report required. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in separate semesters.
courses.prereqText: Consent of course instructor required. Restricted to students enrolled in the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Global Perspectives for Intercultural Learning
courses.description: Prepares students who are going abroad for a semester or academic year for their transition through a) examining expectations, b) focusing on the purpose and value of the abroad experience, c) preparing students culturally and logistically, d) addressing issues of culture shock, e) helping students with articulating their experience for future personal and professional goals, f) enhancing intercultural communication and global understanding, and g) assisting with re-entry planning. May be repeated in separate terms.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Global Perspectives in Cross-Cultural Contexts
courses.description: Provides an opportunity for students studying abroad to consider how their journey might be articulated as a global learning experience. Requires students to discuss what they are learning, reflect upon it, and discern ways to apply the knowledge gained through their experiences. May be repeated in separate terms.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: LAS Study Abroad
courses.description: Provides credit toward the undergraduate degree for study at accredited foreign institutions or approved overseas programs. Final determination of credit is made upon the student's completion of the work. (Summer session, 0 to 8 hours). Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated to a maximum of 36 term hours per academic year or to a total of 44 term hours, all of which must be earned within one calendar year.
courses.prereqText: One year of residence at UIUC, good academic standing, and prior approval of the major department and the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Internships and Professional Experiences
courses.description: Develops career readiness competencies as students engage in professional experiences, such as internships, service learning, volunteer opportunities, or a part-time job. Students connect these professional experiences to both their academic journeys and next steps after graduation. Career development theories are demonstrated and applied, helping students develop lifelong career management competencies. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours. Duration of commitment to professional experience and level of academic involvement are reflected in the number of credit hours enrolled.
courses.prereqText: Instructor approval required. Restricted to students enrolled in a bachelor's degree program in the College of LAS. Students must be concurrently enrolled in some professional experience.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Leadership & Professional Development
courses.description: Leadership and professional development seminar for student interns. Interns will learn teaching, mentoring, leadership and professional skills that will enable them to lead a section of an LAS transition course or experience and share their successful academic experiences with undergraduate students who are new to the University. Interns will help their students develop the skills necessary to succeed at the U of I. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 hours.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Foundations of Academic Research and Creative Activity
courses.description: Success as a scholar requires capabilities that typically are learned not in the classroom, studio, or on stage, but rather as they are encountered over many years. This course accelerates the learning process dramatically by delivering those capabilities prior to the start of one’s career. Topics include types of research and creative activity, public attitudes, how funding opportunities are created, critique, communicating outcomes, ethical conduct, bias, intellectual property, compliance, multidisciplinary inquiry, and collaboration.

courses.subject: LAS
courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: For students seeking graduation with distinction in IPS. 2 or 4 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. May be repeated to a maximum of 4 undergraduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor and IPS Advisory Committee; open only to students whose major is IPS and who have a cumulative grade point average of at least 3.25.
